chapter_theme: A song at Thiruneyththanam (திருநெய்த்தானம்): after a picture of lovemaking, the poet vows that even sleeping in women's embrace he will not forget Murugan's feet; the praise is a battle scene in drum syllables and Siva's dance.

889.reading: The poet describes the lovemaking, cloud-dark hair loosening, garlands slipping, the lotus face sweating, the eyes striking the earrings, coral lips drunk, the musk-scented breasts pressed, and says that even sleeping so in embrace he will not forget Murugan's feet. The praise shows the battle in drum syllables, ghouls rising, Bhairavas and demons dancing with their hunger ended by the vel, names Murugan the son of the Lord who dances to the drum wearing serpents, who embraced the kura girl of the mountain, at Thiruneyththanam, lord of the gods.
889.nuance: துயில்கினும் உனதடி மறவேனே: the song does not renounce the embrace but vows remembrance in the middle of it, an unusual turn for the book. The drum syllables (குகுகுக் கூகுக், செகசெச்) are rhythm.
